boundary: A score is written and the performer chooses. The research kernels do not establish a prior cosmic script, agency, purpose, or literal sound.
explanation: A stable specification can admit different event-by-event realisations while a selected invariant remains readable.
misleading_if: used to imply deterministic scheduling, teleology or independent proof of the substrate
name: A score and many performances

boundary: The map is not a physical metric or spacetime. Relational states are not necessarily places, and paths are sequences of transformations.
explanation: Two processes can occupy the same places with the same frequencies while differing in paths, first-return or passage statistics.
misleading_if: used to claim displacement or gravity from a graph-based first passage
name: A map and its journeys

boundary: Mechanical forces and material solidity are not primitive; being a pictured arch does not establish long-lived organisation.
explanation: A structure maintained by imposed rules differs from one that the same dynamics can sustain for an appreciable lifetime.
misleading_if: used as evidence that a FREE reference already exists
name: Scaffolding and a self-supporting arch

boundary: A braid presupposes geometry and material continuity; graph/hypergraph grammar need not encode either.
explanation: The pattern of relations among constituents can determine outcomes even when simple counts and component strengths match.
maps: same scalar aggregate with different structure
misleading_if: used to assert topological invariants without model proof
name: A braid and its strands

boundary: No claim that human awareness causes physical transitions; a mathematical readout is not a conscious observer.
explanation: An observation channel may retain edges, graph shape, chronology or coarse statistics, and distinct channels can hide different predictive details.
image_suggestion: one scene seen through different lenses
maps: unobserved variables relevant to some futures
misleading_if: used to imply quantum measurement collapse
name: Different lenses on the same landscape

boundary: Physical fluids, geography and conservation mechanisms are analogies, not a derivation from finite relational grammar.
explanation: A system can preserve an overall recurring arrangement even while the exact routes active at one moment change.
misleading_if: used as proof of actual persistence under participant turnover
name: A delta that keeps changing its channels

boundary: Neither instrument establishes physical time's ontology or a gravitational clock rate.
explanation: A process can look different when sampled per unit time versus per event, even with the same underlying transitions.
image_suggestion: stopwatch next to mechanical step counter
misleading_if: used to collapse all time definitions or claim time dilation
name: A stopwatch and a step counter
